title: 3D Benchy
desc: The 3D Benchy is the world's most-printed 3D model and the standard torture test for FDM printers. Designed by Creative Tools, this little tugboat packs overhangs, bridging, curved surfaces, small details, and symmetry checks into one 60mm print. Every new printer, filament, or slicer profile gets validated against a Benchy: stringing shows in the cabin windows, overhang droop on the bow, elephant's foot at the hull base, and layer consistency along the hull. It is the universal benchmark print

title: 20mm XYZ Calibration Cube
desc: The 20mm XYZ calibration cube is the simplest dimensional-accuracy test in 3D printing. A hollow-free 20x20x20mm cube with embossed X, Y, and Z letters lets you verify each axis with calipers: every face should measure 20.00mm within 0.1mm. Skewed dimensions reveal belt tension problems, wrong steps-per-mm, or frame squareness issues. Print it in 20 minutes, measure all three axes, and adjust before committing to long prints. Every printer owner should keep a reference cube from each machine. De

title: Cali Cat
desc: Cali Cat is a cute calibration cat that tests overhangs, bridging, stringing, and fine detail in one friendly 35mm print. Its tail is a steep overhang, the ears test small-feature cooling, and the whisker gaps reveal stringing. Faster and more fun than a cube, it is the go-to first print for dialing in a new filament: one cat per temperature step builds a visual temperature tower of quality. The model prints without supports and finishes in under an hour. Designer: Dezign. License: Open license

title: Temperature Tower
desc: A temperature tower prints the same test geometry at stepped temperatures (e.g., 220C down to 185C in 5C blocks) so you can read the optimal nozzle temperature for any filament off the finished print. Each block is labeled with its temperature; look for the cleanest bridging, sharpest overhangs, and least stringing. This single 2-hour print replaces days of trial and error and is the correct first step with every new spool. G-code post-processing scripts in most slicers automate the temperature

title: Retraction Test (Twin Towers)
desc: The twin-tower retraction test prints two thin pillars with a gap between them, forcing dozens of travel moves. Stringing, blobs, or wisps between the towers reveal retraction distance and speed problems. Tune retraction in 0.5mm steps until the gap is clean. This 15-minute print saves hours of post-processing on real models and is essential when switching between PLA, PETG (stringier), and TPU (minimal retraction). Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: calib

title: Voron 2.4 Printed Parts Set
desc: The Voron 2.4 is a flagship open-source CoreXY 3D printer, and its entire printed-parts set — 87 components including the StealthBurner toolhead, TAP probe mount, gantry joints, and skirt pieces — is released under the GPL. These are functional engineering parts, not decorations: they must be printed in ABS or ASA with high infill for heat resistance inside the enclosed chamber (60C+ ambient). This set is the definitive advanced print project: 60+ hours of printing that ends with a 350mm^3 high-

title: Prusa i3 MK3S+ Printed Parts
desc: Prusa Research prints its own printer parts: the i3 MK3S+ ships with 30+ 3D-printed PETG components (extruder body, X-ends, Y-corners, LCD cover) that Prusa manufactures on its 500+ printer farm in Prague. The STLs are GPL, so anyone can print spares or build a full MK3S+ from the open BOM. PETG is specified for its layer adhesion and temperature resistance. This is the canonical example of 3D printing as real manufacturing — a farm of printers literally reproducing themselves. Designer: Prusa R

title: StealthBurner Toolhead
desc: The StealthBurner is VoronDesign's GPL toolhead for Voron printers: a compact direct-drive extruder with dual 5015 part-cooling fans, Clockwork 2 extruder gears, and an integrated TAP or inductive probe mount. Its 12 printed parts form ducted airflow that cools bridges and overhangs at 300mm/s+ print speeds. As a standalone project it teaches duct design, fan shrouds, and heat management — skills that transfer to any printer mod. Print in ABS/ASA; PLA will soften near the heater block. Designer:

title: Gridfinity Baseplate System
desc: Gridfinity is Zack Freedman's open modular organization system: a 42x42mm grid baseplate with stackable bins in 1x1 to 6x6 unit sizes, all parametric in OpenSCAD. Print baseplates for your drawers and bins for every component — screws, SD cards, tools — and everything snaps into a perfect grid. The system went viral because it solves the universal maker problem: chaotic parts drawers. Baseplates print flat without supports; bins print in vase-friendly walls. Scale the grid to any drawer in the p

title: E-NABLE Phoenix Prosthetic Hand
desc: The e-NABLE Phoenix hand is an open-source 3D-printed prosthetic for below-elbow limb differences, designed by the global e-NABLE volunteer community. Body-powered: wrist flexion drives finger closure through tension cords, giving a functional grip for under $50 in filament versus thousands for commercial devices. Over 10,000 hands have been delivered free to recipients worldwide. Print in PLA with 30%+ infill for strength; assembly needs screws, elastic cord, and padding. This is 3D printing at

title: Montana Mask Frame
desc: The Montana Mask is an open-source 3D-printed respirator frame designed by Dr. Dusty Richardson during the 2020 PPE shortage. It holds a square of surgical mask or furnace-filter material in a sealed frame with a printed filter grille, giving a reusable N95-style seal. Hospitals, makerspaces, and individuals printed hundreds of thousands. The 2-part print takes 3 hours in PLA or PETG; filter material and elastic complete it. A landmark case of distributed emergency manufacturing via desktop 3D p

title: Articulated Crystal Dragon
desc: Cinderwing3D's articulated crystal dragon is the iconic print-in-place flexi toy: dozens of interlocking segments print already assembled, flexing like a real spine straight off the bed. No supports, no assembly — the clearances are engineered into the model. It demonstrates advanced tolerance design (0.3-0.5mm gaps that print separately but stay linked). A perfect showpiece print that proves your printer's dimensional accuracy and makes an unbeatable gift. Print slow with good cooling for crisp

title: Lithophane Photo Panel
desc: A lithophane is a 3D-printed photo: varying the thickness of white PLA (0.8mm to 3mm) encodes image brightness, so the picture appears when backlit. Free lithophane makers convert any photo to a curved or flat STL in seconds. Print in white PLA at 0.1mm layers, 100% infill, standing vertical for best resolution. The result looks like magic — a blank white slab that reveals a portrait in window light. Popular for nightlights, ornaments, and memorial pieces. Designer: Open community technique. Lic

title: Cable Chain (Energy Chain)
desc: Print-in-place cable chains route wires cleanly on 3D printers, CNC machines, and robots. Each link snaps to the next with engineered clearances, forming a flexible chain that guides cables through a controlled bend radius. Print 20+ links flat, snap together, and mount with printed brackets. Sizing is parametric: link inner width must clear your cable bundle plus 20%. A rite-of-passage functional print that makes any machine look professional and protects wiring from fatigue. Designer: Open com

title: Filament Dry Box
desc: Wet filament causes popping, stringing, and weak layers — a dry box fixes it. This printed 6-part design converts a cereal container into a sealed spool holder with PTFE feed tubes, desiccant trays, and a hygrometer window. Print in PETG (moisture resistant), add a $3 cereal container and silica gel, and your nylon/PETG/TPU stays under 20% humidity indefinitely. Essential for anyone printing hygroscopic filaments; pays for itself in saved failed prints. Designer: Open community design. License:

title: Parametric Battery Dispenser
desc: A gravity-feed AA/AAA battery dispenser: load fresh batteries at the top, pull dead ones from the bottom slot. The parametric OpenSCAD source adjusts to any battery size. Three printed parts (body, ramp, front plate) assemble without hardware. Print in PLA with 15% infill; the design uses printed rails instead of fasteners. A perfect first functional print — useful daily, impossible to buy this exact size, and demonstrates parametric design thinking. Designer: Open community design. License: Ope

title: Tool Holder Wall Panel
desc: Modular wall panels with printed hooks, bins, and holders turn any workshop wall into organized storage. The 8-part starter set includes hex-key holders, screwdriver racks, spool mounts, and parts bins that friction-fit into slotted panels. Panels tile to cover any wall area; print more hooks as your tool collection grows. PLA is fine indoors; use PETG near windows (UV). A weekend project that permanently upgrades a workspace. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). G

title: Self-Watering Planter
desc: A 3-part self-watering planter: outer pot, inner soil basket, and water reservoir with a wicking cord. Fill the reservoir monthly; capillary action waters the plant. Print in PETG (water-resistant) with 3+ walls to prevent seepage, and seal the reservoir with food-safe epoxy if needed. The design scales parametrically from succulent pots to herb planters. Combines 3D printing with real horticulture — a living functional print. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). G

title: Cookie Cutter Set
desc: Custom cookie cutters are the classic personalized print: any silhouette becomes a cutter in minutes with free generators. This 5-shape starter set prints with a reinforced 0.8mm cutting edge and comfortable handle. Use food-safe PLA and hand-wash only (layer lines harbor bacteria; never dishwasher). Design your own from any black-and-white image — wedding shapes, logos, pet silhouettes. A 30-minute print that makes every holiday better. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (co

title: Phone Stand (Adjustable)
desc: A 2-part adjustable phone stand with indexed tilt angles from 30 to 75 degrees. The base prints flat, the cradle snaps in with detents — no hardware, no glue. Fits phones with cases up to 12mm thick; the parametric source scales to tablets. Print in PLA with 20% infill; add adhesive rubber feet to stop sliding. The canonical desk-upgrade print: 2 hours, infinitely more useful than the factory box your phone came in. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: house

title: Headphone Stand
desc: A single-piece headphone stand with a wide stable base and curved yoke that cradles the headband without compressing ear pads. Prints without supports in 4 hours; the yoke's 40mm radius fits over-ear headphones from all major brands. Add felt pads to the yoke to protect leather headbands. Variants include under-desk clamp mounts and dual-headset stands. The definitive desk-tidiness print — cheap, fast, and used every single day. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community).

title: Drawer Organizer Grid
desc: Interlocking drawer organizer trays in 6 sizes that tile any drawer with zero wasted space. Each tray prints flat in 2 hours; dovetail edges lock trays together so they never shift. The parametric source regenerates trays to exact millimeter dimensions — measure once, print a perfect fit. Use PLA for desk drawers, PETG for kitchen (heat/steam). Replaces $40 store organizers with $2 of filament cut exactly to your drawers. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group:

title: SD Card Holder
desc: A pocket-size holder for 8 micro-SD cards with labeled slots and a snap-fit lid. Prints in 45 minutes with 0.15mm layers for crisp slot tolerances; cards press in with a satisfying click and never fall out in a bag. Essential for photographers, drone pilots, and Raspberry Pi users juggling a dozen cards. Print in bright colors so it never gets lost in a gear bag. Designer: Open community design. License: Open license (community). Group: workshop. Year: 2018. Parts: 1. Materials: PLA.

title: Raspberry Pi 4 Case
desc: A 3-part ventilated case for the Raspberry Pi 4 with GPIO slot, camera ribbon cutout, and 30mm fan mount. The Pi 4 throttles under load without cooling — this case's chimney vents and optional fan keep it at full clock indefinitely. Prints in 3 hours; brass inserts or printed threads take the M2.5 screws. Dozens of variants exist (stackable, DIN-rail, touchscreen), but this vented 3-piece is the reliable standard every Pi owner should print first. Designer: Open community design. License: Open l
